disposition_reason: Heavy-metal accumulation in wild blueberries (Vaccinium myrtillus) and cowberries from ten Russian regions is shown only in Figures 1 and 2; the text prints no concentrations.

study.design: Survey of wild forest berries from background taiga areas of ten regions
study.origin: Leningrad, Pskov, Novgorod, Vologda, Karelia, Komi, Murmansk, Irkutsk, Tyumen and Yakutia regions, Russia
study.method: X-ray fluorescence spectroscopy (Spectroscan Max G) on air-dry ground berries

unresolved: All values are figure-only (Figures 1 and 2); not read off charts.
Text says cobalt, vanadium and titanium oxide were not detected and manganese oxide was 10-100 times higher than Sr, Pb, As, Zn, Ni and Cr, without numbers.
Cadmium was not reported despite Russian limits being cited for Cd; XRF is a low-sensitivity method for Pb and As in berries.
Methods text says 'blueberries and cranberries were collected' while the species studied are blueberry and cowberry.
